- Dev–Ben–Cara: but wait, if Cara is before Dev, then Ben immediately after Dev and Cara immediately after Ben can't hold as Dev–Ben–Cara. Actually Cara immediately after Ben, Ben immediately after Dev means D–B–C, so Cara would be after Dev. Contradiction unless Cara comes before Dev in a different way… but “Ben immediately after Dev” and “Cara immediately after Ben” force D–B–C order.

That means if Cara is before Dev, the only way out is that “Cara immediately after Ben” is a different Cara than the one in D-B-C? No — there’s only one Cara. So the given statement “Cara has to be scheduled before Dev” must refer to an ordering where it’s still possible overall without breaking constraints… Let’s test if the full set can coexist with Cara before Dev.

Actually from D–B–C, Cara is after Dev. So Cara before Dev contradicts D–B–C. Thus either the note is wrong or it's a different task variant. The task above did not include “Cara before Dev”; the note at the end says “Cara has to be scheduled before Dev”. If we enforce that, the constraints are inconsistent.

But let’s see if there’s another interpretation: maybe Cara can be before Dev if Dev is not immediately before Ben? But “Ben is immediately after Dev” is explicit. That forces the three consecutive D-B-C, so Cara > Dev. So no schedule satisfies Cara before Dev here.
